title: MLflow — What it is
description: MLflow (created at Databricks, now LF AI & Data) manages machine learning end to end: Tracking logs parameters, metrics and artifacts per run; Projects package code for reproducible execution; Models standardize packaging across flavors (sklearn, pytorch, onnx); and the Model Registry stages versions from Staging to Production with lineage. mlflow ui serves the dashboard locally on port 5000. It is made by Databricks / LF AI & Data and runs on Windows, macOS, Linux (Python).

title: MLflow — Configuration essentials
description: MLflow is configured through a small, explicit surface: `mlflow.tracking_uri`, `mlflow.registry`, `mlflow.experiment`. The demo below validates a sample configuration against the required keys, because most MLflow failures are configuration mistakes, and a validator catches them before they cost time.
facts: The Model Registry moves versions through Staging, Production and Archived stages.
MLflow Projects define reproducible runs via MLproject files and conda/docker envs.
Recipes (pipelines) template common ML workflows.
demo_code:
required = ['mlflow.tracking_uri', 'mlflow.registry', 'mlflow.experiment']
sample = {
    'mlflow.tracking_uri': './mlruns',
    'mlflow.registry': 'sqlite:///registry.db',
    'mlflow.experiment': 'default',
}
print('CONFIG VALIDATION')
ok = True
for k in required:
    good = k in sample and sample[k] not in (None, '')
    ok = ok and good
    print(f"  [{'PASS' if good else 'FAIL'}] {k} = {sample.get(k)!r}")
print('RESULT:', 'valid configuration' if ok else 'INVALID')
demo_output:
CONFIG VALIDATION

  [PASS] mlflow.registry = 'sqlite:///registry.db'

title: MLflow — Data formats and portability
description: Portability is a feature: MLflow works with MLmodel YAML, Conda env YAML, Run artifacts. The demo below proves the round-trip — serialize a sample record, parse it back, verify byte-for-byte equality — because data you cannot move is data you do not own.

import json
record = {'tool': 'MLflow', 'format': 'MLmodel YAML', 'n': 1}
blob = json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True)
back = json.loads(blob)
assert back == record, 'round-trip mismatch'
print('serialize  :', blob)
print('round-trip : OK (byte-identical)')
print('formats archived: ' + 'MLmodel YAML, Conda env YAML, Run artifacts')

title: MLflow — Troubleshooting
description: When MLflow misbehaves, diagnose in order: re-check configuration, re-run the entry command `mlflow.start_run()` (open a tracking run), then inspect the data formats for corruption. The demo below encodes this decision tree so the most common failures resolve to a concrete next step.
facts: MLflow was created at Databricks and donated to the Linux Foundation.
mlflow.start_run() opens a run; log_param/log_metric record to it.
mlflow.sklearn.log_model() packages a scikit-learn model in MLflow format.
demo_code:
tree = [("won't start", 're-run entry command: mlflow.start_run() (open a tracking run)'), ('wrong behavior', 'validate config keys: mlflow.tracking_uri, mlflow.registry, mlflow.experiment'), ("can't find data", 'check MLmodel YAML files exist in expected paths'), ('slow', 'reduce scope, then consult performance record (ladder 13)')]
symptom = 'wrong behavior'
print('DIAGNOSTIC DECISION TREE')
for s, fix in tree:
    mark = '>>>' if s == symptom else '   '
    print(f'{mark} if {s}: {fix}')
print('diagnosis for', repr(symptom), '->', [f for s, f in tree if s == symptom][0])
